title: Spin lifetime anisotropy in graphene induced by the SiO2 interface
summary: Understanding how common dielectric substrates influence the spin transport properties of graphene is essential for advancing graphene-based spintronic technologies. Here we use a comprehensive set of numerical simulations to reveal how a SiO$_2$ substrate modifies the spin texture and governs spin relaxation in graphene. Using first-principles density matrix dynamics simulations, as well as tight-binding (TB) transport simulations, we quantify the effects of electron-phonon scattering, impurity scattering, and electrostatic disorder on the spin relaxation process. We find that a 2D SiO$_2$ substrate induces a predominantly Rashba-type helical spin texture in graphene, leading to a spin lifetime anisotropy of 1/2. Meanwhile, bulk SiO$_2$ breaks in-plane symmetry in graphene, leading to anisotropic in-plane and out-of-plane components in the spin texture, which we capture with a newly-developed TB model of graphene. Transport simulations under realistic disorder conditions reveal a spin lifetime anisotropy between 0.5 and 1, similar to what is seen in measurements of graphene spin valves on a SiO$_2$ substrate. Our results reveal a more complex picture of spin relaxation at the ubiquitous graphene/SiO$_2$ interface, beyond the standard Rashba model, providing critical insight for interpreting experiments and guiding substrate engineering for graphene spintronics.

AI.tldr: This paper uses first-principles density matrix dynamics and tight-binding transport simulations to show that SiO2 substrates induce Rashba-type helical spin textures in graphene with anisotropic spin lifetimes (0.5–1), revealing a more complex spin relaxation picture at the graphene/SiO2 interface than the standard Rashba model predicts.
AI.motivation: Understanding how common dielectric substrates influence spin transport in graphene is essential for advancing graphene-based spintronic technologies, yet the role of SiO2 substrates in modifying spin texture and relaxation was not fully understood beyond simplified Rashba descriptions.
AI.method: The authors combine first-principles density matrix dynamics simulations with tight-binding (TB) transport simulations to quantify the effects of electron-phonon scattering, impurity scattering, and electrostatic disorder on spin relaxation. They also develop a new TB model to capture the anisotropic in-plane and out-of-plane spin texture components induced by bulk SiO2.
AI.result: A 2D SiO2 substrate induces a predominantly Rashba-type helical spin texture in graphene with a spin lifetime anisotropy of 1/2, while bulk SiO2 breaks in-plane symmetry producing anisotropic spin texture components. Transport simulations under realistic disorder show spin lifetime anisotropies between 0.5 and 1, consistent with experimental measurements on graphene spin valves.
AI.conclusion: The spin relaxation at the graphene/SiO2 interface is more complex than the standard Rashba model predicts, providing critical insight for interpreting experiments and guiding substrate engineering for graphene spintronics.

title: Data-Efficient Adaptation of DPA-4 Force Fields to DFT+U Energetics: A Case Study in NiO
summary: Foundation machine-learned force fields (MLFFs) are often pretrained on broad materials datasets whose electronic-structure conventions may not reproduce the phase energetics required for a specific correlated material. Using NiO as a case study, we examine whether incorrect source-level phase energetics can be corrected efficiently through target-level fine-tuning. Along a common structural interpolation, non-spin-polarized PBE and ferromagnetic PBE+U predict opposite energetic orderings of the octahedral Oct and square-planar Sqr phases. Pretrained DPA-4 models adapt rapidly to the NiO PBE+U surface, reaching energy and force root-mean-square errors (RMSEs) of approximately 0.5 meV/atom and 30 meV/Å, respectively, with approximately 170 PBE+U labels. Crucially, models previously fine-tuned to the opposing no-U surface recover the qualitative PBE+U phase ordering with nearly the same target-data efficiency as models fine-tuned directly from their respective pretrained initializations. Our results show that incorrect source-level phase energetics can be reversed through target-level fine-tuning, and suggest a practical multi-fidelity strategy in which pretraining prioritizes broad, consistent, and affordable data, while compact target-level datasets impose energetics through application-specific fine-tuning.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates whether incorrect phase energetics in pretrained machine-learned force fields (MLFFs) can be corrected via target-level fine-tuning, using NiO as a case study. Despite source-level non-spin-polarized PBE data predicting opposite phase ordering compared to PBE+U, fine-tuned DPA-4 models recover the correct PBE+U energetics with only ~170 labels (RMSE ~0.5 meV/atom, ~30 meV/Å). Even models fine-tuned from an opposing no-U surface match the target-data efficiency of directly fine-tuned models.
AI.motivation: Pretrained MLFFs built on broad datasets may encode electronic-structure conventions whose phase energetics are incompatible with specific correlated materials. The authors ask whether such incorrect source-level energetics can be efficiently corrected through target-level fine-tuning, rather than requiring full re-pretraining.
AI.method: Using NiO as a case study, the authors compare structural energetics along an interpolation between octahedral (Oct) and square-planar (Sqr) phases under non-spin-polarized PBE (opposing ordering) vs. ferromagnetic PBE+U (correct ordering). They fine-tune DPA-4 models—both directly from pretrained initializations and from models previously fine-tuned to the opposing no-U surface—on PBE+U labels and measure energy/force RMSE and phase-ordering recovery.
AI.result: Directly fine-tuned DPA-4 models reach ~0.5 meV/atom and ~30 meV/Å RMSE with ~170 PBE+U labels. Models fine-tuned from the opposing no-U surface recover the qualitative PBE+U phase ordering with nearly the same target-data efficiency as models fine-tuned directly from their pretrained initializations, demonstrating that incorrect source-level energetics can be reversed through target-level fine-tuning.
AI.conclusion: Incorrect source-level phase energetics in pretrained MLFFs can be corrected via application-specific fine-tuning with compact datasets. This supports a multi-fidelity strategy where pretraining emphasizes broad, consistent, affordable data while fine-tuning imposes target-specific energetics.

title: Large bias-tunable magnetoresistance from spin-dependent interlayer hybridization in van der Waals antiferromagnet CrSBr-based heterostructures
summary: We explore the large magnetoresistance (MR) in \ce{hBN}/few-layer-graphene/\ce{CrSBr}/few-layer-graphene heterostructures and reveal the mechanism behind its non-monotonic bias dependence. Using bias voltage and temperature as independent tuning knobs, we achieve MR up to \SI{350}{\percent} at \SI{20}{K}, characterized by symmetric M-shaped maxima around $\pm 0.5\,\mathrm{V}$. Continuous tuning of the magnetization angle $θ$ via a hard-axis magnetic field shows that the barrier band-edge offset varies linearly with $\cos(θ/2)$, a first-order signature of spin-dependent interlayer hybridization. This linear relationship rules out the Jullière model and a spin-filter projection. We conclude that the magnetic-configuration-dependent band edge, rather than electrode spin polarization, dictates the large magnetoresistance in \ce{CrSBr} junctions.

AI.tldr: The paper explores large magnetoresistance (up to 350% at 20K) in hBN/few-layer-graphene/CrSBr/few-layer-graphene heterostructures, revealing that the mechanism is based on magnetic-configuration-dependent band-edge offset (linear in cos(θ/2)) rather than electrode spin polarization, ruling out the Jullière model and spin-filter projection.
AI.motivation: To understand the mechanism behind the non-monotonic bias dependence of large magnetoresistance in CrSBr-based heterostructures, specifically to determine whether the effect arises from electrode spin polarization (Jullière-type) or from magnetic-configuration-dependent band edges in the barrier material.
AI.method: Fabrication of hBN/few-layer-graphene/CrSBr/few-layer-graphene heterostructures, using bias voltage and temperature as independent tuning knobs, and continuous tuning of magnetization angle θ via a hard-axis magnetic field to probe the angular dependence of the barrier band-edge offset.
AI.result: Achieved MR up to 350% at 20K with symmetric M-shaped maxima around ±0.5 V. The barrier band-edge offset varies linearly with cos(θ/2), a first-order signature of spin-dependent interlayer hybridization, ruling out the Jullière model and spin-filter mechanisms.
AI.conclusion: The large magnetoresistance in CrSBr junctions is dictated by the magnetic-configuration-dependent band edge of the barrier rather than electrode spin polarization.

title: Geometry of Noisy Quantum Many-Body Dynamics with Continuous Symmetries: Entanglement and Correlations
summary: We study unitary quantum dynamics in noisy Brownian models with global continuous symmetries, such as $U(1)$ and $SU(2)$, focusing on Rényi entanglement entropies and hydrodynamic and non-hydrodynamic correlators. By mapping the averaged late-time dynamics to the low-energy physics of effective replica Hamiltonians, we find that the evolution is controlled by the quantum geometry of their ground-state manifolds, which is directly related to the geometry of $k$-commutants---the symmetry algebra of $k$ replicas of the system. In interacting systems, these $k$-commutants are generically determined solely by the symmetries of the system, independent of microscopic details of the noisy evolution. This allows us to use the time-dependent variational principle (TDVP) to provide simple geometric explanations for the sub-ballistic Rényi entanglement growth and the anomalous decay of non-hydrodynamic correlators in interacting systems with continuous symmetries. We find this behavior to be intimately connected to singularities within the $k$-commutant manifolds, arising from frozen ``void'' states in the Hilbert space that exist due to continuous on-site symmetries. This also demystifies the important role of voids in the dynamics of these observables, previously identified in $U(1)$ symmetric systems. We compare these behaviors in interacting systems with Abelian and non-Abelian continuous symmetries and in free-fermion systems, which differ in the geometry of their $k$-commutants. Ultimately, this work provides a general geometric framework for systematically studying observables in noisy systems with continuous symmetries, including Haar-random circuits.

AI.tldr: This paper studies noisy Brownian quantum dynamics with continuous global symmetries (U(1), SU(2)), showing that late-time Rényi entanglement growth and non-hydrodynamic correlator decay are governed by the quantum geometry of k-commutant manifolds. In interacting systems, the geometry is set by symmetries alone, and singularities ("voids") in these manifolds explain sub-ballistic entanglement growth and anomalous correlator decay.
AI.motivation: To develop a general geometric framework for understanding how continuous symmetries control the late-time dynamics of observables (entanglement entropy and correlators) in noisy quantum systems, and to explain the previously mysterious role of "void" states in U(1)-symmetric systems.
AI.method: The authors map averaged late-time dynamics to low-energy physics of effective replica Hamiltonians. The ground-state manifolds are related to k-commutants (symmetry algebra of k replicas). They use the time-dependent variational principle (TDVP) to derive geometric explanations for dynamical behavior, connecting singularities in k-commutant manifolds to frozen void states induced by continuous on-site symmetries.
AI.result: For interacting systems, k-commutants are determined solely by the symmetries, independent of microscopic details. Sub-ballistic Rényi entanglement growth and anomalous decay of non-hydrodynamic correlators are geometrically explained via singularities in k-commutant manifolds. The framework distinguishes Abelian vs non-Abelian continuous symmetries and free-fermion systems, which differ in k-commutant geometry.
AI.conclusion: This work provides a general, systematic geometric framework for studying observables in noisy systems with continuous symmetries (including Haar-random circuits), unifying and demystifying the role of voids and providing predictive power across different symmetry and interaction classes.

title: Second-Derivative-Corrected FANPT for Robust Continuation of Nonlinear Wavefunction Equations
summary: We present a second-derivative-corrected extension of the Flexible Ansatz for N-body Perturbation Theory (FANPT) for solving nonlinear Flexible Ansatz for N-body Configuration Interaction (FANCI) wavefunction equations. The original quasilinear FANPT approximation neglects second- and higher-order derivatives of the determinant overlap with respect to wavefunction parameters. In this work, we retain the overlap Hessian and neglect only third- and higher-order parameter derivatives, thereby including the leading nonlinear response of the wavefunction ansatz while preserving the same response-matrix structure used in the original FANPT formulation. The resulting additional terms enter only through the constant vector of the response equations and are implemented for coupled-cluster wavefunctions in the FanPy/FANCI framework. The new approximation is tested on the Lithium Hydride molecule and the insertion of Beryllium into H$_2$ using seniority-restricted coupled-cluster wavefunctions in the STO-6G basis. The main advantage of the second-derivative correction is that it provides a better initial guess for solving the projected FANCI equations at the next point along the adiabatic connection. This improvement is diagnosed by comparing the FANPT-propagated parameters with the independently optimized FANCI parameters at the same value of $λ$. For nonlinear coupled-cluster ansatzes, especially when larger $λ$-steps are used, the corrected approximation reduces the same-$λ$ parameter deviations and suppresses large parameter-space excursions. These results show that the leading nonlinear overlap correction improves the reliability of FANPT as a continuation strategy for nonlinear wavefunction equations.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a second-derivative-corrected extension of FANPT (Flexible Ansatz for N-body Perturbation Theory), which retains the overlap Hessian (neglecting only third- and higher-order parameter derivatives) to include the leading nonlinear response of the wavefunction ansatz while preserving the original FANPT response-matrix structure. Implemented for coupled-cluster wavefunctions in the FanPy/FANCI framework, the correction improves the initial guess for solving projected FANCI equations along the adiabatic connection, as demonstrated on LiH and Be+H2 in the STO-6G basis.
AI.motivation: The original quasilinear FANPT approximation neglects second- and higher-order derivatives of the determinant overlap with respect to wavefunction parameters, limiting its accuracy as a continuation strategy for nonlinear wavefunction equations. This work aims to include the leading nonlinear response (the overlap Hessian) to improve the reliability of FANPT as a continuation method.
AI.method: The authors retain the overlap Hessian in the FANPT expansion while neglecting only third- and higher-order parameter derivatives. The additional terms enter through the constant vector of the response equations, preserving the same response-matrix structure as original FANPT. The approach is implemented for coupled-cluster wavefunctions in the FanPy/FANCI framework and tested on LiH and Be insertion into H2 using seniority-restricted coupled-cluster wavefunctions in the STO-6G basis.
AI.result: The second-derivative correction provides a better initial guess for solving the projected FANCI equations at the next point along the adiabatic connection. For nonlinear coupled-cluster ansatzes, especially with larger λ-steps, the corrected approximation reduces same-λ parameter deviations and suppresses large parameter-space excursions compared to the original FANPT.
AI.conclusion: The leading nonlinear overlap correction improves the reliability of FANPT as a continuation strategy for nonlinear wavefunction equations, making it a more robust approach for solving projected FANCI equations along the adiabatic connection.

title: Temperature-Driven Sequential Modeling for the Prediction of Annual Power Conversion Efficiency Profiles of Organic Photovoltaic Materials: Douala Case Study
summary: Organic photovoltaic (OPV) materials are promising candidates for distributed solar energy in tropical regions, yet existing virtual screening tools report static power conversion efficiency (PCE) values at standard testing conditions (STC) that fail to capture the temperature-driven performance degradation experienced under real deployment conditions. Here we introduce a Climate-Native computational framework that forecasts the annual PCE profile of OPV donor molecules under geographically realistic operating conditions. The framework combines GFN2-xTB molecular dynamics with an equivariant graph neural network surrogate ($268$ Neyman-stratified CEP molecules; $120,600$ training geometries; $\sim 1050\times$ speedup over explicit quantum chemistry) and sequential deep learning models trained on annual time series anchored in NASA POWER climate data for Douala, Cameroon, and validated by zero-shot transfer to Yaoundé and Maroua. Applied to $\sim 30,000$ molecules from the Harvard Clean Energy Project (CEP) and validated against $350$ HOPV15 experimental device measurements, the framework demonstrates that sequential models trained on full molecular dynamics trajectories outperform time-averaged baselines ($35\%$-$48\%$ relative MAE improvement over static baselines), confirming that thermal conformational dynamics carry information beyond mean geometry. We further introduce a seasonal stability score that reranks OPV candidates by performance consistency under tropical conditions, identifying molecules whose deployment suitability differs substantially from their static PCE ranking.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a Climate-Native computational framework for forecasting annual power conversion efficiency (PCE) profiles of organic photovoltaic (OPV) donor molecules under real tropical operating conditions. Combining GFN2-xTB molecular dynamics with an equivariant graph neural network surrogate and sequential deep learning models anchored in NASA POWER climate data, the framework demonstrates that temperature-driven performance degradation can be captured, with sequential models on full MD trajectories outperforming static baselines by 35%-48% relative MAE. A seasonal stability score is introduced to rerank OPV candidates by performance consistency in tropical climates, identifying molecules whose deployment suitability diverges from static PCE rankings.
AI.motivation: Existing virtual screening tools for OPV materials report static PCE values at standard testing conditions (STC), which fail to capture temperature-driven performance degradation under real deployment conditions, particularly in tropical regions where OPV is a promising candidate for distributed solar energy.
AI.method: The framework combines GFN2-xTB molecular dynamics with an equivariant graph neural network surrogate (trained on 268 Neyman-stratified CEP molecules and 120,600 training geometries, achieving ~1050x speedup over explicit quantum chemistry), followed by sequential deep learning models trained on annual time series anchored in NASA POWER climate data for Douala, Cameroon, with zero-shot validation on Yaoundé and Maroua. Applied to ~30,000 molecules from the Harvard Clean Energy Project and validated against 350 HOPV15 experimental device measurements.
AI.result: Sequential models trained on full molecular dynamics trajectories outperform time-averaged baselines by 35%-48% relative MAE improvement over static baselines, confirming that thermal conformational dynamics carry information beyond mean geometry. A seasonal stability score was introduced to rerank OPV candidates by performance consistency under tropical conditions, identifying molecules whose deployment suitability substantially differs from their static PCE ranking.
AI.conclusion: Thermal conformational dynamics encode information critical for accurate PCE prediction under real-world tropical conditions; static PCE rankings can misrepresent deployment suitability, and the proposed climate-native framework with seasonal stability scoring provides a more reliable route for OPV candidate selection in tropical regions.

title: Quetzalcoatlite as a Disorder-Free Platform for Chiral Magnetism and Frustration
comment: 9 Pages, including 6 Figures, and additional four pages of Supplementary Information
summary: The natural mineral quetzalcoatlite Zn$_6$Cu$_3$(TeO$_6$)$_2$(OH)$_6$ $\cdot$ (Ag$_x$Pb$_y$Cl$_{x+2y}$) is a structurally ideal kagome magnet, providing a platform for exploring the interplay of geometric frustration, chirality, and tunability in a disorder-free framework. Here, we present the (first) comprehensive ab initio study of its electronic and magnetic properties. The electronic structure is dominated by localized half-filled Cu $d_{x^2-y^2}$ orbitals that become insulating through electronic correlations. Mapping the low-energy physics onto a Heisenberg model reveals that the magnetism is governed primarily by two exchange interactions: a nearest-neighbor intralayer kagome coupling and a next-nearest-neighbor interlayer coupling. Their competition stabilizes an unconventional three-dimensional chiral magnetic state. Each kagome layer hosts a $\sqrt{3}\times\sqrt{3}$ order, while adjacent layers are rotated by $60^\circ$, producing a right-handed spiral along the crystallographic $c$-axis. This intrinsic chiral order emerges naturally from the crystal structure and magnetic interactions, establishing quetzalcoatlite as a distinctive realization of chiral magnetism on a perfect kagome lattice. At the same time, the small energy scale of the exchange interactions places the material close to competing magnetic regimes, suggesting that moderate pressure, chemical substitution, or structural modifications may strongly enhance frustration, suppress long-range order, and potentially drive the system toward a quantum spin-liquid state.

AI.tldr: First comprehensive ab initio study of the natural kagome magnet quetzalcoatlite, revealing localized half-filled Cu d-orbitals, a two-interaction Heisenberg model, and an intrinsic three-dimensional chiral magnetic state with √3×√3 in-plane order and a right-handed spiral along the c-axis. Small exchange energy scales suggest tunability toward a quantum spin-liquid regime.
AI.motivation: Quetzalcoatlite is a structurally ideal kagome magnet that provides a disorder-free platform to explore geometric frustration, chirality, and tunability, yet its electronic and magnetic properties have not been comprehensively studied from first principles.
AI.method: Comprehensive ab initio calculations of the electronic structure, mapping of low-energy physics onto a Heisenberg model, and determination of the dominant exchange interactions (nearest-neighbor intralayer kagome coupling and next-nearest-neighbor interlayer coupling).
AI.result: The material is an insulator driven by electronic correlations of localized half-filled Cu d_{x^2-y^2} orbitals. The competition between the two dominant exchange interactions stabilizes an unconventional three-dimensional chiral magnetic state: each kagome layer exhibits √3×√3 order with adjacent layers rotated by 60°, forming a right-handed spiral along the c-axis. The small exchange energy scale places the material near competing magnetic regimes.
AI.conclusion: Quetzalcoatlite is a distinctive intrinsic realization of chiral magnetism on a perfect kagome lattice. Moderate pressure, chemical substitution, or structural modifications may enhance frustration, suppress long-range order, and potentially drive the system toward a quantum spin-liquid state.

title: Unifying Physical Backpropagation
summary: Physical computing systems exploit device dynamics for computation, but their gradient-based optimization is challenging: backpropagation through a digital twin suffers from model-reality gap. On-device gradient computation could resolve this issue, and a handful of theoretical and experimental studies have proposed ways to achieve it. Yet a unifying theory identifying when a physical system can compute the gradient of its own performance has been missing. Here we develop such a unification, based on the adjoint method: we identify sufficient conditions under which the adjoint field required for formally exact gradients can be generated on the same hardware that performs the computation. Linear and nonlinear systems obey fundamentally different conditions: for linear systems damping or gain is admissible provided reciprocity is preserved. For nonlinear trajectory systems the sufficient conditions are reciprocity of the linearized system and the existence of a time-reversal mirror. Algorithmically, the nonlinear case requires infinitesimal nudging, whereas linear systems admit a finite-amplitude experiment. We recover Equilibrium Propagation, Hamiltonian echo backpropagation, fully forward mode training and in situ gradient methods in integrated-photonic and free-space-optical systems. We further show that reciprocity is only the simplest instance of a more general intertwining condition, which extends exact on-device gradient computation to a class of non-Hermitian, non-reciprocal systems. Further generalizations include time-dependent parameters, Onsager-reciprocal dynamics and nonlinear, PT-symmetric Schrödinger equations. Our work provides a unified theoretical basis for formally exact physical learning algorithms and a template for constructing them across a range of physical systems.

AI.tldr: This paper develops a unifying theory, based on the adjoint method, for when a physical computing system can compute the exact gradient of its own performance on-device. It identifies sufficient conditions—reciprocity for linear systems, and reciprocity of the linearized system plus a time-reversal mirror for nonlinear trajectory systems—and shows that existing methods like Equilibrium Propagation, Hamiltonian echo backpropagation, and fully forward mode training are special cases of this framework.
AI.motivation: Gradient-based optimization of physical computing systems is challenging because backpropagation through digital twins suffers from model-reality gaps. While on-device gradient computation has been proposed in scattered theoretical and experimental works, a unifying theory identifying when a physical system can compute the gradient of its own performance was missing.
AI.method: The authors use the adjoint method to derive sufficient conditions under which the adjoint field required for formally exact gradients can be generated on the same hardware performing the computation. They distinguish linear from nonlinear systems, formulate conditions (reciprocity for linear systems; reciprocity of linearized system plus time-reversal mirror for nonlinear trajectory systems), and introduce a more general intertwining condition that extends exact on-device gradient computation to non-Hermitian, non-reciprocal systems.
AI.result: The framework recovers established methods including Equilibrium Propagation, Hamiltonian echo backpropagation, fully forward mode training, and in situ gradient methods in integrated-photonic and free-space-optical systems. It also extends to time-dependent parameters, Onsager-reciprocal dynamics, and nonlinear PT-symmetric Schrödinger equations. Algorithmically, nonlinear cases require infinitesimal nudging while linear systems admit finite-amplitude experiments.
AI.conclusion: The work provides a unified theoretical basis for formally exact physical learning algorithms and serves as a template for constructing such algorithms across diverse physical systems.

title: Discriminating superconducting fluctuations from the pseudogap in Bi$_2$Sr$_2$Ca$_{n-1}$Cu$_n$O$_{2n+4+δ} (n = 2,3)$: A magnetotransport study
comment: 7 pages 4 figures in the main manuscript; 9 pages 9 figures in the Supplemental Material
summary: Understanding the normal state is essential for uncovering the mechanism of high-$T_c$ superconductivity. We investigate magnetotransport in Bi$_2$Sr$_2$CaCu$_2$O$_{8+δ}$ and Bi$_2$Sr$_2$Ca$_2$Cu$_3$O$_{10+δ}$ single crystals over a wide doping range. While the in-plane resistivity and Hall coefficient show strong pseudogap-induced temperature dependence, the $T^2$ Hall-angle behavior and the modified Kohler's rule remain robust across all dopings. The onset temperatures of the pseudogap are clearly distinct from superconducting fluctuations, although they scale with the pseudogap magnitudes with a factor consistent with a $d$-wave superconductor. These results demonstrate that the pseudogap does not arise from superconducting fluctuations and instead suggest that it may originate from preformed Cooper pairing in the BCS-BEC crossover regime.

AI.tldr: The paper investigates magnetotransport in Bi2Sr2CaCu2O8+δ and Bi2Sr2CaCu2O10+δ single crystals across a wide doping range. While in-plane resistivity and Hall coefficient show strong pseudogap-induced temperature dependence, the T² Hall-angle behavior and modified Kohler's rule remain robust. The onset temperatures of the pseudogap are distinct from superconducting fluctuations but scale with pseudogap magnitudes in a manner consistent with a d-wave superconductor. The authors conclude the pseudogap does not arise from superconducting fluctuations and may originate from preformed Cooper pairing in the BCS-BEC crossover regime.
AI.motivation: Understanding the normal state is essential for uncovering the mechanism of high-Tc superconductivity, and the pseudogap phase is a key unresolved feature in cuprate superconductors.
AI.method: Magnetotransport measurements (in-plane resistivity and Hall coefficient) were performed on Bi-based cuprate single crystals (Bi-2212 and Bi-2223) across a wide doping range, analyzing Hall-angle behavior, Kohler's rule, and the temperature dependence of pseudogap-related quantities.

The pseudogap onset temperature is distinct from superconducting fluctuation temperature scales, though they scale together with a factor consistent with a d-wave superconductor.

title: A Frequency-Space Terahertz Transceiver Chip for Multi-Agent Communications and Spatial Awareness
summary: Future indoor embodied-intelligence systems require scalable hardware platforms that support both high-capacity multi-agent connectivity and mutual spatial awareness. The terahertz (THz) spectrum offers abundant bandwidth and inherent spatial selectivity for integrated sensing and communication (ISAC); however, conventional phased arrays and programmable metasurfaces rely on dense beamforming networks, element-level control, or external THz illumination, making scalable multibeam operation challenging. Here, we report a fully integrated 208-258GHz 65-nm CMOS THz transceiver chip that monolithically integrates broadband front ends with heterogeneous leaky-wave metasurface (HLM) apertures within a 1.5mm by 4.9mm area. The HLM generates strongly dispersive leaky modes, enabling 75 degree frequency-controlled beam scanning with only four meta-atoms. Co-design of frequency-domain and spatial-domain mixing achieves spectrally clean frequency-to-space mapping for spatial-frequency division multiple access (SFDMA) communication. The THz chip demonstrates multi-agent simultaneous transmission and reception, two-dimensional localization, and sensing-enhanced communication, providing a scalable hardware platform for future THz embodied-intelligence networks.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a fully integrated 208-258 GHz 65-nm CMOS THz transceiver chip that monolithically integrates broadband front ends with heterogeneous leaky-wave metasurface (HLM) apertures in a compact 1.5mm × 4.9mm area. The HLM enables 75° frequency-controlled beam scanning with only four meta-atoms, achieving spectrally clean frequency-to-space mapping for spatial-frequency division multiple access (SFDMA) communication. The chip demonstrates multi-agent simultaneous transmission/reception, 2D localization, and sensing-enhanced communication, offering a scalable hardware platform for THz embodied-intelligence networks.
AI.motivation: Future indoor embodied-intelligence systems require scalable hardware platforms supporting both high-capacity multi-agent connectivity and mutual spatial awareness. Conventional phased arrays and programmable metasurfaces rely on dense beamforming networks, element-level control, or external THz illumination, making scalable multibeam operation challenging. The THz spectrum offers abundant bandwidth and inherent spatial selectivity for ISAC, motivating a compact, scalable hardware solution.

The HLM generates strongly dispersive leaky modes enabling 75° frequency-controlled beam scanning with only four meta-atoms. AI.conclusion: The proposed THz transceiver chip provides a scalable hardware platform for future THz embodied-intelligence networks, overcoming the scaling limitations of conventional beamforming approaches by leveraging frequency-controlled metasurface apertures for integrated sensing and communication.

title: Analytically Consistent Reconstruction of Finite Data Using Padé Sequences
summary: Reconstructing the analytic structure of a function from finite datasets is a fundamental problem across theoretical, numerical, and experimental physics. While Padé approximants provide a natural framework, finite-information effects, as well as statistical and systematic uncertainties, may obscure the underlying analytic structure and limit reconstruction reliability. In this work, we reinterpret the appearance of Froissart doublets not merely as numerical artifacts but as \textit{diagnostic objects} carrying information about the analytic consistency of the input data. Accordingly, we develop a general Padé-based algorithm that exploits the dynamics of Froissart doublets along Padé sequences to identify localized inconsistencies and iteratively reconstruct the analytic structure most compatible with the data. The method requires no model for the origin of the inconsistencies and distinguishes genuine analytic features from spurious structures induced by finite-information effects. We validate it using Stieltjes functions, realistic pseudo-experimental datasets with statistical and systematic uncertainties, and general holomorphic functions. The complete algorithm is provided as a supplementary Mathematica notebook in an open GitLab repository.

AI.tldr: This paper develops a Padé-based algorithm that interprets Froissart doublets as diagnostic objects rather than mere numerical artifacts, using their dynamics along Padé sequences to detect and correct localized inconsistencies in finite data and reconstruct the underlying analytic structure of functions without a prior model for the inconsistency source.
AI.motivation: Reconstructing the analytic structure of a function from finite datasets is a fundamental problem in physics, but finite-information effects and statistical/systematic uncertainties obscure the true analytic structure and limit the reliability of standard Padé approximation approaches.
AI.method: A general Padé-based algorithm that tracks the dynamics of Froissart doublets across Padé sequences to identify localized inconsistencies in input data, then iteratively reconstructs the most data-compatible analytic structure. It requires no model for the origin of the inconsistencies.
AI.result: The method is validated using Stieltjes functions, realistic pseudo-experimental datasets with statistical and systematic uncertainties, and general holomorphic functions. The complete algorithm is released as a supplementary Mathematica notebook in an open GitLab repository.
AI.conclusion: Froissart doublets can be repurposed as diagnostic tools for analytic consistency, enabling robust analytic structure reconstruction from imperfect data without prior knowledge of the inconsistency mechanism.

title: Compact Actively-Shielded Magnetic Field Coil within Mu-Metal Shields for ACME Electric Dipole Moment Measurements
summary: A system of actively-shielded coils and mu-metal shields is devised, constructed and shown to provide the stable and spatially uniform magnetic field needed for the ACME III electron electric dipole moment (eEDM) measurement. Two layers of current-carrying coils, enclosed within three layers of ferromagnetic shields, produce a field that varies by less than 1 nT (10 $\uG$) within the 1 m $\times$ 4.2 cm $\times$ 4.2 cm interior volume in which a beam of ThO molecules are probed as they precess. The demountable shields are constructed from rectangular mu-metal plates. The largest, with a mass of 19 kg and an area of 2.18 m $\times$ 0.75 m, is easily carried by two people and just fits within a large available annealing oven. The assembly design facilitates low-stress mounting and handling to suppress changes in the magnetic properties of the mu metal, and also provides modular access to apparatus within the coils for maintenance and upgrades. The nearly static external ambient field is reduced within the shielded precession volume by up to a factor of $10^5$. During the magnetic field reversals that ACME uses to suppress systematic uncertainties, the ``actively-shielded'' coil largely cancels out its external fringing field to minimize the magnetization of the mu metal. Even though the shields are only 10 cm outside the coils, shield degaussing after every magnetic field reversal is not required. The non-reversing residual field stays below 1 nT for up to 17 hours when the field is reversed every 30 seconds, for example. The measured performance, compared to the previous generation ACME II apparatus, suggests that the magnetic-field-related systematic uncertainties for ACME III will be smaller by an estimated factor of 40 despite a five times longer precession volume and the use of three magnetic shielding layers rather than five.

AI.tldr: This paper describes the design, construction, and performance of a magnetic shielding and active coil system for the ACME III electron electric dipole moment (eEDM) experiment. The system achieves a spatially uniform magnetic field varying by less than 1 nT over the 1 m × 4.2 cm × 4.2 cm precession volume, reduces external ambient fields by up to 10^5, and eliminates the need for degaussing after field reversals, resulting in a factor of 40 reduction in magnetic-field-related systematic uncertainties compared to ACME II.
AI.motivation: The ACME III experiment requires a highly stable and spatially uniform magnetic field for measuring the electron electric dipole moment using a beam of ThO molecules. A reliable magnetic shielding system is needed to reduce external field interference and suppress systematic uncertainties, while also being practical to construct, handle, and maintain.
AI.method: The system uses two layers of current-carrying coils enclosed within three layers of ferromagnetic (mu-metal) shields. The shields are constructed from demountable rectangular mu-metal plates, designed for low-stress mounting to preserve magnetic properties and provide modular access. An actively-shielded coil cancels external fringing fields during field reversals, and shield degaussing is not required after each reversal. Performance is compared to the previous ACME II generation with five shielding layers.
AI.result: The constructed system produces a field varying by less than 1 nT within the 1 m × 4.2 cm × 4.2 cm interior volume, reduces external ambient fields by up to a factor of 10^5, and maintains a non-reversing residual field below 1 nT for up to 17 hours with 30-second field reversals. Compared to ACME II, magnetic-field-related systematic uncertainties are estimated to be smaller by a factor of 40 despite a five times longer precession volume and fewer shielding layers (three versus five).
AI.conclusion: The actively-shielded coil and three-layer mu-metal shield design successfully meets the stringent magnetic field requirements for the ACME III eEDM measurement, achieving superior performance over the previous generation with practical, modular construction and without the need for degaussing after field reversals.

title: Layer-Number-Controlled Symmetry Breaking and Surface-State Transport in Rhombohedral Graphene Multilayers
summary: Rhombohedral multilayer graphene hosts layer-polarized flat bands, providing an intriguing platform for correlated and topological electronic states; however, the role of layer number in governing symmetry breaking and surface screening remains elusive. Here we prepare rhombohedral graphene multilayers and systematically conduct electrical transport measurements. We uncover an unconventional layer dependence of phase transitions: the critical displacement field (D$_{c}$) for the layer-antiferromagnetic (LAF)-to-semimetal transitions remains constant across tetralayer to hexalayer graphene, whereas the D$_{c}$ for semimetal-to-layer-polarized-insulator (LPI) transition increases with layer number, defying unscreened Coulomb interaction models. In hexalayer graphene, surface-state-dominated transport emerges, with Landau levels (LLs) and resistive peaks selectively controlled by adjacent gates, a signature of strong interlayer screening absent in thinner stacks. High magnetic fields reveal valley-layer-locked LLs and dissipative states possibly from interlayer backscattering, highlighting the presence of decoupled surface states. Our findings establish layer number as a key tuning knob for engineering correlated and topological phases in rhombohedral graphene multilayers.

AI.tldr: This paper studies rhombohedral multilayer graphene (tetralayer to hexalayer) via electrical transport, revealing unconventional layer-dependent phase transitions: the critical displacement field for layer-antiferromagnetic-to-semimetal transitions is constant, while that for semimetal-to-layer-polarized-insulator transitions increases with layer number. Hexalayer graphene exhibits surface-state-dominated transport with gate-selectable Landau levels and resistive peaks due to strong interlayer screening, and high fields reveal valley-layer-locked Landau levels with dissipative interlayer backscattering states.
AI.motivation: Rhombohedral multilayer graphene hosts layer-polarized flat bands that are promising for correlated and topological electronic states, but the role of layer number in governing symmetry breaking and surface screening has remained elusive. Understanding this layer dependence is crucial for engineering these phases.
AI.method: The researchers prepared rhombohedral graphene multilayers and systematically conducted electrical transport measurements across tetralayer, pentalayer, and hexalayer graphene, examining phase transitions as a function of displacement field and layer number, along with magnetotransport measurements at high magnetic fields.
AI.result: Discovered unconventional layer dependence: Dc for LAF-to-semimetal transitions is constant across layer thicknesses, while Dc for semimetal-to-LPI transitions increases with layer number (contradicting unscreened Coulomb models). In hexalayer graphene, surface-state-dominated transport emerges with gate-selective control of Landau levels and resistive peaks. High fields reveal valley-layer-locked LLs and dissipative states possibly from interlayer backscattering, indicating decoupled surface states.
AI.conclusion: Layer number is established as a key tuning parameter for engineering correlated and topological phases in rhombohedral graphene multilayers. The strong interlayer screening and decoupled surface states found in thicker stacks provide new opportunities for controlling electronic states in these systems.

title: Operational identifiability of false-vacuum decay rates in the quantum Ising chain
summary: Extracting a thermodynamic nucleation rate from finite-time quantum dynamics requires separating observable decay from estimator and finite-size validity. We develop a multilevel identification framework to real-time tensor-network simulations of false-vacuum decay in the one-dimensional quantum Ising chain. Across twelve parameter points with non-empty analysis intervals, the same coherent two-kink amplitudes semi-quantitatively predict both infinite-chain survival and magnetization dynamics: the survival coefficient has a median lattice-to-theory ratio of 0.902, while the magnetization-area slope ratios span 0.809--0.953. By contrast, the microscopic nearest-neighbour bond response is coherence dominated: vacuum--pair coherence contributes 60.0--81.5\% within the seven parameter points satisfying the matched-bond-dimension convergence criterion, while substantial late-window slope discrepancies remain that cannot be removed by a scalar normalization. The framework establishes reliable finite-time decay coefficients and identifies the additional finite-size and branch-validation requirements for a bulk thermodynamic rate interpretation. Within the two-kink model, a lattice-resolved WKB action reduces the median fixed-prefactor discrepancy with the coherent-bubble spectral calculation to 4.13\%. Quantitative cross-level consistency, observable-dependent reduced-model error, and a thermodynamic-rate interpretation that remains subject to finite-size validation can therefore coexist.

AI.tldr: A multilevel identification framework for real-time tensor-network simulations extracts finite-time decay coefficients for false-vacuum decay in a 1D quantum Ising chain, separating observable decay from estimator and finite-size validity, and demonstrates quantitative cross-level consistency while identifying requirements for a bulk thermodynamic rate interpretation.
AI.motivation: Extracting a thermodynamic nucleation rate from finite-time quantum dynamics is difficult because observable decay must be separated from estimator and finite-size validity effects.
AI.method: Develops a multilevel identification framework applied to real-time tensor-network simulations of false-vacuum decay in the one-dimensional quantum Ising chain, using coherent two-kink amplitudes to predict survival and magnetization dynamics, analyzing nearest-neighbour bond response coherence, and comparing lattice-resolved WKB actions with coherent-bubble spectral calculations.
AI.result: Across twelve parameter points, coherent two-kink amplitudes semi-quantitatively predict survival and magnetization dynamics (survival coefficient median ratio 0.902; magnetization-area slope ratios 0.809-0.953). Vacuum-pair coherence contributes 60.0-81.5% of nearest-neighbour bond response across seven valid parameter points, with late-window slope discrepancies not removable by scalar normalization. Lattice-resolved WKB action reduces median fixed-prefactor discrepancy to 4.13%.
AI.conclusion: The framework establishes reliable finite-time decay coefficients and identifies finite-size and branch-validation requirements for a bulk thermodynamic rate interpretation. Quantitative cross-level consistency, observable-dependent reduced-model error, and a thermodynamic-rate interpretation subject to finite-size validation can coexist.

title: A Perspective on Phase Space Electronic Structure Theory : From Its Surface Hopping Origins Through To Its Future Promise
summary: We trace the history of phase space electronic structure theory (PSEST), high- lighting how this powerful approach emerged from fundamental questions in semi- classical surface hopping dynamics and evolved into an alternative to standard Born- Oppenheimer based electronic structure theory (with moving instead of frozen nuclei). Our goal herein is not to recapitulate the mathematical details of phase space electronic structure calculations, and few equations are presented so as to maximize readability. Instead, our goal is to provide intuition for those new to the field both (i) regarding the physics present when solving the Schrodinger equation in a non-inertial frame as well as (ii) regarding why PSEST is a necessary step forward towards understanding chemical problems involving spin (with limited practical alternatives). We further high- light some of the many open questions in this fast developing area, which will hopefully inspire new practitioners in this field. This intuitive perspective lacks many equations and is meant to complement (rather than replace) the more technical review given in Bian et al, Chem. Phys. Rev. 7, 011303 (2026)

AI.tldr: A non-technical, intuitive review of phase space electronic structure theory (PSEST), tracing its origins from semiclassical surface hopping dynamics and explaining its physics, motivation (especially for spin-related chemical problems), and open questions, complementing a more technical companion review.
AI.motivation: PSEST has emerged as an alternative to standard Born-Oppenheimer-based electronic structure theory, incorporating moving rather than frozen nuclei. The authors aim to provide intuition for newcomers about the physics of solving the Schrodinger equation in a non-inertial frame and why PSEST is a necessary step forward, particularly for chemical problems involving spin, given limited practical alternatives.
AI.method: A narrative/historical perspective rather than a technical derivation. The paper traces the evolution of PSEST from semiclassical surface hopping dynamics, presents few equations, and focuses on providing physical intuition about non-inertial frame quantum mechanics, the role of spin, and open questions in the field.
AI.result: The paper offers a readable, intuitive account of why PSEST is needed, its physical underpinnings in non-inertial frames, and its particular relevance to spin-related chemistry, while enumerating several open questions to motivate new practitioners.
AI.conclusion: PSEST is a promising, fast-developing alternative to standard Born-Oppenheimer theory, especially for spin-related chemical problems, and this perspective serves as an accessible complement to the technical review by Bian et al. (Chem. Phys. Rev. 7, 011303 (2026)) aimed at inspiring further research.

title: Chemically Meaningful Textualization Enables Explainable Validation of Metal-Organic Frameworks by Large Language Models
summary: Computation-ready metal-organic framework (MOF) databases are essential for high-throughput screening, yet many reported crystal structures remain chemically unreasonable or disordered, compromising simulation fidelity. Existing validation approaches can identify non-computation-ready structures, but they often rely on heuristic rules, license requirement, or offer limited interpretability. Here, we show that large language models (LLMs) can serve as interpretable validators of MOF structures when crystallographic information is transformed into chemically meaningful text. By benchmarking nine descriptors, we find that successful LLM-based validation depends not on the amount of structural information alone, but on whether local coordination, framework connectivity, and chemical context are organized into a linguistically learnable representation. Fine-tuned LLMs using specialized descriptors (mof2text) achieve performance comparable to graph-based models in identifying unreasonable MOFs. Importantly, these models extend beyond black-box classification by generating diagnostic rationales for likely error sources, including abnormal bonding, connectivity, and charge states, as well as error-category predictions for annotated datasets. This work establishes chemically informed textualization as the key step that transforms LLMs from generic text models into practical and explainable tools for curating MOF databases.

AI.tldr: This paper demonstrates that large language models (LLMs) can serve as interpretable validators of metal-organic framework (MOF) structures when crystallographic data is converted into chemically meaningful text representations. Fine-tuned LLMs with specialized descriptors (mof2text) achieve performance comparable to graph-based models while providing diagnostic rationales for structural errors, establishing chemically informed textualization as the key step for transforming LLMs into practical tools for MOF database curation.
AI.motivation: Computation-ready MOF databases are essential for high-throughput screening, but many reported crystal structures are chemically unreasonable or disordered, compromising simulation fidelity. Existing validation approaches rely on heuristic rules, have license requirements, or offer limited interpretability, creating a need for more accessible and explainable validation methods.
AI.method: The authors transform crystallographic information into chemically meaningful text and benchmark nine descriptors for LLM-based MOF validation. They identify that successful validation depends on whether local coordination, framework connectivity, and chemical context are organized into a linguistically learnable representation. They fine-tune LLMs using specialized descriptors (mof2text) and compare performance against graph-based models.
AI.result: Fine-tuned LLMs using specialized mof2text descriptors achieve performance comparable to graph-based models in identifying unreasonable MOFs. Additionally, these models generate diagnostic rationales for likely error sources including abnormal bonding, connectivity, and charge states, as well as error-category predictions for annotated datasets, extending beyond black-box classification.
AI.conclusion: Chemically informed textualization is the key step that transforms LLMs from generic text models into practical and explainable tools for curating MOF databases, offering both comparable accuracy to graph-based methods and valuable interpretability through diagnostic rationales.

title: The Fate of Crystalline Topological Phenomena in the Continuum
summary: The continuum limit is a widely used theoretical construct for obtaining continuum field-theories of crystalline systems. We study the formulation of a continuum limit for gapped bosonic phases and ask whether their topological properties survive passage to the continuum. Using methods in algebraic topology and category theory, we give a rigorous formulation of the continuum limit and construct a surjective global map relating crystalline topological phases across all finite point-group symmetries to continuum invertible topological phases. Consequently, we find that some lattice phases admit no continuum limit, while distinct lattice phases that do admit a continuum limit can share the same continuum image, hence implying that some lattice topological data can collapse. Conversely, we find that every continuum invertible phase admits a faithful crystalline realization. In addition to the general framework, we apply it to several examples, including studies of a 2D rotation-symmetric phase, higher-order topological phases, and the mixed spin-lattice anomaly of the deconfined quantum critical point between an antiferromagnet and valence bond solid.

AI.tldr: This paper rigorously formulates the continuum limit for gapped bosonic crystalline topological phases using algebraic topology and category theory, showing that topological data can collapse or be lost in the continuum limit, while every continuum invertible phase admits a faithful crystalline realization.
AI.motivation: The continuum limit is a standard theoretical construct for deriving continuum field theories from crystalline systems, but whether topological properties survive this passage has been unclear. The authors aim to rigorously determine which lattice topological phases admit a continuum limit and whether the mapping preserves or collapses topological information.
AI.method: The authors use methods from algebraic topology and category theory to construct a rigorous formulation of the continuum limit. They build a surjective global map relating crystalline topological phases across all finite point-group symmetries to continuum invertible topological phases, and apply this framework to several concrete examples.
AI.result: The authors find that some lattice phases admit no continuum limit at all, while distinct lattice phases that do admit a continuum limit can map to the same continuum phase, implying lattice topological data can collapse. Conversely, every continuum invertible phase admits a faithful crystalline realization. Applications include a 2D rotation-symmetric phase, higher-order topological phases, and the mixed spin-lattice anomaly of the deconfined quantum critical point between an antiferromagnet and valence bond solid.
AI.conclusion: The continuum limit of gapped bosonic crystalline topological phases is not injective—topological distinctions among lattice phases can be lost—and some lattice phases cannot be described by any continuum field theory. However, the map is globally surjective onto continuum invertible phases, ensuring every continuum invertible phase can be realized on a lattice.

title: Logarithmically Correlated Landscapes and Localization in Non-Hermitian Quasicrystals
summary: We study a one-dimensional Hatano-Nelson ring whose nonreciprocal hopping is quasiperiodically modulated through zero. A gauge transformation maps every eigenstate onto a single spatial envelope, whose logarithm becomes a deterministic, logarithmically correlated field once the hopping vanishes along the quasiperiodic orbit. We derive an exact Fourier representation and prove that the landscape variance grows logarithmically with system size, with a stiffness set by the modulation power and the arithmetic of the incommensurate frequency. The extended phase terminates at an algebraic boundary given by Jensen's formula. Inside the singular regime, localization requires the stiffness to exceed a critical threshold: above it, the wavefunction weight concentrates on the few highest landscape peaks and the state is localized; below it, the weight spreads over too many competing peaks and the state is a critical multifractal. The extreme-value statistics are anomalous: peak gaps grow as a power of the logarithm of rank, with an exponent that encodes the continued-fraction type of the frequency, distinct from the Anderson, Aubry-André, and random-gauge universality classes. The stiffness adds across channels in multiband lattices, and all signatures survive percent-level component disorder, placing the mechanism within reach of nonreciprocal topolectrical circuits.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes a one-dimensional Hatano-Nelson ring with quasiperiodically modulated nonreciprocal hopping that passes through zero. A gauge transformation maps eigenstates onto a single spatial envelope whose logarithm forms a deterministic, logarithmically correlated field. The landscape variance grows logarithmically with system size with a stiffness set by modulation power and frequency arithmetic. The extended phase terminates at an algebraic boundary given by Jensen's formula. Localization requires a critical stiffness threshold, above which weight concentrates on few landscape peaks (localized) and below which states are critical multifractals. Extreme-value statistics reveal anomalous peak-gap scaling with exponents encoding continued-fraction type, distinct from Anderson, Aubry-André, and random-gauge classes. The mechanism survives percent-level disorder and is accessible in nonreciprocal topolectrical circuits.
AI.motivation: To understand novel localization-delocalization transitions in systems combining nonreciprocity (Hatano-Nelson) with quasiperiodic modulation that vanishes, and to establish a new universality class for extreme-value statistics in such systems distinct from known Anderson and Aubry-André classes.
AI.method: The authors use a gauge transformation to map all eigenstates to a single spatial envelope whose logarithm becomes a deterministic, logarithmically correlated field (Gaussian-like free field structure). They derive an exact Fourier representation, prove logarithmic growth of landscape variance with a stiffness parameter controlled by modulation power and the arithmetic of the incommensurate frequency, employ Jensen's formula to locate the algebraic extended-phase boundary, analyze stiffness thresholds for localization versus critical multifractality, and study extreme-value statistics of landscape peaks encoding continued-fraction arithmetic.
AI.result: The landscape variance grows logarithmically with system size with a stiffness set by modulation power and incommensurate-frequency arithmetic. The extended phase terminates at an algebraic boundary given by Jensen's formula. Above a critical stiffness, states localize onto the few highest landscape peaks; below it, states are critical multifractals. Peak gaps grow as a power of the logarithm of rank with an exponent encoding the continued-fraction type of the frequency, distinct from known universality classes. Stiffness adds across channels in multiband lattices, and all signatures survive percent-level component disorder.
AI.conclusion: The work identifies a new mechanism and universality class for localization in quasiperiodic nonreciprocal systems, where the logarithmically correlated envelope field governs both localization thresholds and anomalous extreme-value statistics. The mechanism is experimentally accessible in nonreciprocal topolectrical circuits, since all predicted signatures are robust to percent-level disorder.

title: Light induced superconducting diode effect in patterned films
summary: Structured light offers a route to control superconducting transport without permanently modifying the material or applying a static bias. Here we show that structured optical driving can generate a superconducting diode response in patterned superconducting films with asymmetric holes. Using generalized time-dependent Ginzburg Landau simulations, we find that optical driving produces rectified dc photovoltages and zero bias directional supercurrent imbalance in a junction free geometry, with continuous-drive diode efficiencies of order $10^{-3}$ and pulsed efficiencies reaching $10^{-2}$. The response is controlled by both the hole array and the optical mode. Increasing the number of asymmetric holes enhances rectification, reversing circular helicity reverses the diode polarity, and the optical spatial mode strongly modifies the magnitude and polarity of the directional response. Pulsed excitation enhances the zero bias line cut current imbalance to the percent level. For linearly polarized illumination, the asymmetric metacrystal converts the drive into local chiral supercurrent motion, inducing an inverse Faraday effect like mechanism for dynamical time reversal symmetry breaking. These results establish patterned superconducting films as a viable platform for light-tunable superconducting diode behavior.

AI.tldr: Structured optical driving can generate a superconducting diode response in patterned superconducting films with asymmetric holes, producing rectified dc photovoltages and zero-bias directional supercurrent imbalance without a junction, with diode efficiencies of order 10^-3 (continuous) to 10^-2 (pulsed).
AI.motivation: To control superconducting transport non-invasively using light (structured optical driving) rather than permanent material modification or static bias, and to demonstrate a tunable superconducting diode effect in a junction-free geometry.
AI.method: Generalized time-dependent Ginzburg-Landau (TDGL) simulations of patterned superconducting films containing asymmetric hole arrays, driven by structured optical modes (continuous and pulsed) with varying helicity and spatial mode profiles.
AI.result: Optical driving yields rectified dc photovoltages and zero-bias directional supercurrent imbalance; continuous-drive diode efficiencies ~10^-3 and pulsed efficiencies ~10^-2. Increasing asymmetric holes enhances rectification, reversing circular helicity reverses diode polarity, and optical spatial mode modulates magnitude and polarity. Linearly polarized light induces local chiral supercurrent motion via an inverse Faraday-like mechanism, enabling dynamical time-reversal symmetry breaking.
AI.conclusion: Patterned superconducting films with asymmetric holes constitute a viable platform for light-tunable superconducting diode behavior, offering contact-free, non-invasive optical control of directional transport.

title: Measurement of third-order elastic constants using thermal modulation of ultrasonic waves
comment: 1. Corrected a sign typo in Eq. (6d) relative to the original APL publication. 2. The final TOEC values might be affected by minor temperature variations during testing; for further discussion, see Zhu et al., Nondestructive Testing and Evaluation, 41(7), 4066-4089 (2026), DOI: 10.1080/10589759.2025.2551866
summary: Third-order elastic constants (TOEC) play an important role in nonlinear material characterization, but measurements of TOEC are laborious with large error margins. This Letter presents the equations of wave velocity changes caused by homogeneous temperature variation and uniaxial stress in isotropic media and the expression of TOEC in terms of thermally induced velocity change and thermal strain. TOEC of an aluminum sample were experimentally determined by measuring ultrasonic wave velocity changes in the uniaxial loading test and the thermal modulation test. Experimental results showed good agreement between the two test methods. Owing to the simple test setup and high measurement sensitivity, the thermal modulation test is a potential experimental method to determine TOEC and absolute acoustic nonlinearity parameters.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a thermal modulation method for determining third-order elastic constants (TOEC) by measuring ultrasonic wave velocity changes due to temperature variation, offering a simpler and more sensitive alternative to traditional uniaxial loading tests.
AI.motivation: TOEC are important for nonlinear material characterization, but traditional measurement methods are laborious and have large error margins, necessitating a simpler and more accurate alternative.
AI.method: The authors derived equations relating wave velocity changes to homogeneous temperature variation and uniaxial stress in isotropic media, expressed TOEC in terms of thermally induced velocity change and thermal strain, and experimentally determined TOEC of aluminum using both uniaxial loading and thermal modulation ultrasonic tests.
AI.result: The TOEC values obtained from the thermal modulation test showed good agreement with those from the uniaxial loading test, demonstrating the validity of the proposed method.
AI.conclusion: Due to its simple test setup and high measurement sensitivity, the thermal modulation test is a promising experimental method for determining TOEC and absolute acoustic nonlinearity parameters.

title: Dynamics of the spontaneous emission factor in multiple quantum well nanowire lasers
summary: The spontaneous emission factor - often known as the \b{eta} factor - is an important quantity in the description of quantum well lasers, influencing both the threshold power as well as the general shape of the light in-light out (L-L) curve. Past work on modelling multiple quantum well (MQW) nanowire laser devices has typically assumed that the \b{eta} factor is a constant parameter that can either be estimated or fit in a post-hoc manner. However, the \b{eta} factor can be derived from the transitions between valence and conduction bands in semiconductor quantum wells, together with knowledge of the cavity modes. Here we investigate the dynamic nature of the \b{eta} factor for MQW nanowire lasers, and show how it can be computed. We also examine the dependence of the spontaneous emission rate and spontaneous emission factor \b{eta} on the charge carrier density, quantum well thickness, and composition, and discuss the impact on laser threshold and operation.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates the dynamic nature of the spontaneous emission factor (β factor) in multiple quantum well (MQW) nanowire lasers, deriving it from valence-conduction band transitions and cavity modes, and examining its dependence on charge carrier density, quantum well thickness, and composition, along with its impact on laser threshold and operation.
AI.motivation: Past work on MQW nanowire lasers has typically treated the β factor as a constant parameter that is estimated or fitted post-hoc. This paper aims to move beyond this assumption by deriving the β factor from fundamental semiconductor physics—transitions between valence and conduction bands in quantum wells together with cavity mode knowledge—and by revealing its dynamic (carrier-dependent) nature rather than treating it as a static constant.
AI.method: The β factor is derived from the transitions between valence and conduction bands in semiconductor quantum wells combined with knowledge of the cavity modes. The paper computes the β factor dynamically and examines the dependence of spontaneous emission rate and the β factor on charge carrier density, quantum well thickness, and composition.
AI.result: The study demonstrates how the β factor for MQW nanowire lasers can be computed from first principles, reveals its dynamic dependence on parameters such as charge carrier density, quantum well thickness, and composition, and discusses the resulting impact on laser threshold power and the shape of the L-L curve and overall laser operation.
AI.conclusion: The β factor in MQW nanowire lasers is not a constant but a dynamically varying quantity that depends on charge carrier density, quantum well geometry, and material composition. Properly computing it from band-to-band transitions and cavity modes provides a more accurate description of device behavior, particularly regarding threshold power and the L-L curve, than previously used constant-parameter fitting approaches.

title: A piston-like polymer stochastic heat engine
summary: Colloidal stochastic engines are often regarded as microscopic analogues of macroscopic pis ton cylinder heat engines. However, although they share some underlying physical principles, such systems remain far from being direct force generators from a practical perspective. Motivated by this limitation, the present study introduces a polymer-based stochastic engine that more closely mimics the operation of piston cylinder engines. In this setup, heat is converted into work through a cyclic process in which a polymer is pulled into and out of a narrow channel under varying tem peratures. The work performed by the engine can be directly obtained from the cyclic trajectory in the force position diagram, analogous to the pressure volume diagram in traditional heat engines. Despite its much higher number of degrees of freedom compared to colloidal engines, the polymer en gine nevertheless follows several characteristic features observed in such systems. Numerical results demonstrate consistency with universal low-dissipation bounds for e ciency, recovery of Carnot e ciency under regeneration, and low-dissipation scaling of work and power.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces a polymer-based stochastic engine that mimics piston-cylinder heat engines by cyclically pulling a polymer into and out of a narrow channel under varying temperatures. Work is extracted from the force-position diagram, analogous to the pressure-volume diagram. Despite higher degrees of freedom than colloidal engines, it obeys universal low-dissipation bounds, achieves Carnot efficiency under regeneration, and exhibits low-dissipation scaling of work and power.
AI.motivation: Colloidal stochastic engines are microscopic analogues of macroscopic piston-cylinder heat engines, but they are not practical direct force generators. The study aims to introduce a polymer-based stochastic engine that more closely mimics the operation of piston-cylinder engines while overcoming this practical limitation.
AI.method: A polymer is cyclically pulled into and out of a narrow channel under varying temperatures, converting heat into work. Work is directly obtained from the cyclic trajectory in the force-position diagram, analogous to the pressure-volume diagram in traditional heat engines. Numerical simulations are used to test performance against universal thermodynamic bounds.
AI.result: Despite having many more degrees of freedom than colloidal engines, the polymer engine reproduces characteristic features: it satisfies universal low-dissipation bounds for efficiency, recovers Carnot efficiency under regeneration, and shows low-dissipation scaling of work and power.
AI.conclusion: The polymer-based stochastic engine provides a more faithful microscopic analogue of piston-cylinder engines while retaining key thermodynamic properties of stochastic engines, such as low-dissipation bounds and Carnot recovery under regeneration, making it a promising practical force-generating microscopic heat engine.

title: Relativistic Dirac-Coulomb-Breit Four-Component Multireference Perturbation Theory within the Small Tensor Product Distributed Active Space Framework
summary: We present a four-component multireference second-order perturbation theory (4C-MRPT2) within the small tensor product distributed active space (STP-DAS) framework. The formulation is compatible with the Dirac-Coulomb (DC), Dirac-Coulomb-Gaunt (DCG), and Dirac-Coulomb-Breit (DCB) Hamiltonians, and inherits the memory-efficient and massively parallel STP-DAS algorithm, enabling perturbative treatments over very large external spaces. Benchmark calculations on noble-gas and group-13 atoms demonstrate that 4C-MRPT2 efficiently recovers all-electron dynamic correlation while providing new insight into relativistic correlation effects. The calculations show that the Breit contribution to the correlation energy increases rapidly with atomic number and reaches approximately 4% of the total correlation energy for Xe. The method also shows that second-order correlation energies are only weakly dependent on the choice of multiconfigurational reference orbitals, and that frozen-core and frozen-virtual approximations substantially reduce computational cost with minimal loss of accuracy.

AI.tldr: The paper presents a four-component multireference second-order perturbation theory (4C-MRPT2) implemented within the small tensor product distributed active space (STP-DAS) framework, compatible with Dirac-Coulomb, Dirac-Coulomb-Gaunt, and Dirac-Coulomb-Breit Hamiltonians. Benchmarks on noble-gas and group-13 atoms show efficient recovery of all-electron dynamic correlation, with Breit contributions reaching ~4% of total correlation energy for Xe.
AI.motivation: To extend multireference perturbation theory to fully relativistic four-component treatments capable of handling very large external spaces, enabling accurate and scalable all-electron dynamic correlation calculations for heavy elements where relativistic and correlation effects are strongly intertwined.
AI.method: A four-component MRPT2 is formulated within the STP-DAS framework, compatible with DC, DCG, and DCB Hamiltonians, leveraging the memory-efficient and massively parallel STP-DAS algorithm for perturbative treatment over large external spaces.
AI.result: Benchmark calculations on noble-gas and group-13 atoms show 4C-MRPT2 efficiently recovers all-electron dynamic correlation. The Breit contribution to correlation energy grows rapidly with atomic number, reaching ~4% for Xe. Second-order correlation energies are weakly dependent on multiconfigurational reference orbital choice, and frozen-core/frozen-virtual approximations greatly reduce cost with minimal accuracy loss.
AI.conclusion: 4C-MRPT2 within the STP-DAS framework provides a scalable, accurate method for fully relativistic dynamic correlation, revealing significant Breit contributions to correlation energy for heavy elements and validating cost-reduction strategies without compromising accuracy.

title: Strain-controlled magnetism and magnetoelasticity in monolayer NiPS$_3$ and CrPS$_4$
summary: We develop a first-principles framework for magnetoelastic coupling in two-dimensional magnets based on a strain-dependent Heisenberg model. In this approach, strain derivatives of the exchange interactions provide direct access to magnetostriction and to the magnetic renormalization of the elastic tensor, establishing a microscopic link between spin interactions and elastic response. We apply the method to monolayer NiPS$_3$ and CrPS$_4$, which exhibit contrasting magnetoelastic behavior. NiPS$_3$ shows weak and nearly isotropic spin-lattice coupling, consistent with a robust zigzag antiferromagnetic ground state. In contrast, CrPS$_4$ displays strong anisotropic coupling, leading to strain-driven transitions between spin-spiral and ferromagnetic phases and significant changes in the critical temperature and elastic response. Our results demonstrate a general route to quantify magnetoelastic effects in low-dimensional magnets and highlight CrPS$_4$ as a promising platform for strain engineering of magnetic order.

AI.tldr: The paper develops a first-principles framework for studying magnetoelastic coupling in 2D magnets using a strain-dependent Heisenberg model, applied to monolayer NiPS3 and CrPS4. It finds weak isotropic coupling in NiPS3 and strong anisotropic coupling in CrPS4, where strain can drive spin-spiral to ferromagnetic phase transitions, highlighting CrPS4 as a platform for strain engineering of magnetism.

title: Thermodynamic Spectroscopy of Emergent Excitations in Quantum Spin Ice
